Garlic has been widely promoted for use in the treatment of hyperlipidaemia (p.1169). Several early place- bo-controlled trials1,2 and meta-analyses3,4 showed that garlic significantly decreased total serum-cholesterol concentrations. However, more recent data suggest that the effect is at best modest5 or that there is no significant difference6-9 when com- pared with placebo. 1. Jain AK, et al.
